title: The client side
description:
Write the user-mode side: build requests, check results and report errors clearly.

```
open \\.\XenonEcho -> ok (simulated)
echo "hello" -> "hello" (5 bytes)
echo 5000 bytes -> refused before sending: more than the 4096 limit
driver not loaded -> "could not open the device: is the driver started?"
```
hints: Checking on both sides is not wasted work: the client's check gives a better message, the driver's check keeps the system safe (lesson 16.06).
`GetLastError()` after a failed `CreateFileW` tells "not found" (2) from "access denied" (5).
requirements: A `Device` class wrapping open, close and `ioctl(code, input, outputSize)` (simulated here; `CreateFileW` and `DeviceIoControl` on Windows).
Check sizes on the client side too, before sending.
Turn failures into messages a person can act on.
stretch: Run many echo requests from several threads at once.
